newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks kick off week on buoyant note.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks kick off week on buoyant note.

text.p: Austrian shares started the week off on a buoyant note with the ATX index of 21 blue chips gaining 1.44 percent to end a shade off the day's high.
Traders said buying was encouraged by firm European bourses and are optimistic the ATX index is headed for higher domains -- the next target being 1,130 points.
"I see the ATX testing new highs for the year," said one trader.
But another said: "The market's performance over the year has been good, so I doubt much more will happen." He added that the market is well supported at 1,110 points.
The ATX jumped 15.9 points to end at 1,124.58 on Monday, just off the session high of 1,124.73 and well above the low of 1,108.64. Of its constituents, 18 advanced while three fell.
Insurer EA-Generali was the day's best performer after the finance ministry said the group had topped up its bid for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt.
EA-Generali surged 5.26 percent on the news to close at 200 schillings, largely in a technical reaction to last week's losses.
"EA-Generali is back in the race," said a trader.

The group headed by the insurer offered to buy 74 percent of the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt, and wants to place the rest on the open market with the help of Union Bank of Switzerland.
"It helps that UBS is taking part...." said another trader.
The day's leading decliner was Wiener Staedtische, down 0.61 percent to 975 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index gained 4.75 points, or 1.13 percent, to 424.62.
The January ATX future added on 16 points to 1,124 on turnover of 1,809 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 254
